sources.name: Sports Illustrated, 'Tallest NBA Players of 2025–26 (and All Time)' (table taken from the NBA's official roster listings)
sources.measures: Official NBA listed height, without shoes (the league has required barefoot measurements since 2019-20), for players on 2025-26 rosters. Gives the ten tallest players, not the full distribution.
sources.notes: Values are in inches, converted from feet and inches as published. Listed heights at the top: Wembanyama 7'4" (88 in); Edey and Zikarsky 7'3" (87 in); Clingan, Porzingis and Kessler 7'2" (86 in); Gobert, Holmgren, Lively and Lopez 7'1" (85 in). The source does not publish a percentile. The p99 figure comes from ranking players: about 530-570 players appear on 2025-26 rosters, so the top 1% is about the 5-6 tallest, and the cutoff falls at 7'2" (86 in, 218.4 cm). The article gives two different counts of 7-footers (42 and 10) and does not explain the difference. Published 2026-06-08.

definition: Official NBA listed height, without shoes (the league has required barefoot measurements since 2019-20), for players on 2025-26 rosters. Gives the ten tallest players, not the full distribution.
caveat: Neither source is independent: both rest on the NBA's own listed heights, through SI and Basketball-Reference. No official NBA publication or peer-reviewed paper gives height percentiles for the whole league. The p99 is a rank cutoff on a small population of roughly 550 players, so it amounts to the sixth or so tallest player, and it moves by a full inch depending on who is counted (two-way and G League call-ups such as Zikarsky). Wembanyama's height is disputed: some reports say the Spurs listed him at 7'5" for 2025-26. Comparison on a different population: a peer-reviewed summary of ten years of NBA Draft Combine data (PMC10593457) gives 197.7 ± 7.6 cm, range 181.6-212.7 cm. That covers draft prospects, not league players. The suggested value is about 218 cm (7'2"), with 221 cm (7'3") as the upper bound.
